$comment: PEMO resident-portal NON-SEVERITY palette. Values are DATA, not source: no hex literal appears in any hand-written .ts/.tsx/.css file, and test/tokens/no-hardcoded-hex.test.ts enforces that. The seven severity levels are NOT here — they are read from severity.json (one copy, nothing to drift).
title: PEMO resident-portal non-severity design tokens
source: PEMO_UI_Design_System_v2.0 sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5. Section 2 is a Proposed baseline, not Accepted; a consumer of a Proposed section inherits an unapproved dependency, and this file says so rather than treating it as settled. See DIVERGENCES.md: the normative source (design-system section 2) is neither machine-readable nor in the repository, so the parity hub below is a TRANSCRIPTION and all three surfaces can agree and all three be wrong together.
whyThisFileExists: severity.json carries severity colour only — seven levels of strong/surface/border. It carries no brand violet, no neutral ramp, no page ground and no divider, and a portal shell cannot be drawn without them. The rule 'a hex in a component is a defect' is kept in substance by keeping these values as DATA and generating the only source that reads them, exactly as UI-019-ST did for the management web.
theRuleThisEncodes: Two copies with nothing deciding which is real is the disease; two copies with an enforced equality check is a cache. The defect was never duplication — it was silence. test/tokens/palette-parity.test.ts is that check.
placementDebt: This is the THIRD surface to carry shared design vocabulary inside a surface-specific home, after the resident-mobile Dart theme and the management-web palette.json. It cannot move: the shared home is packages/**, which this PID may not write. Two boundary-crossers was debt; three is a pattern. UI-028-ST raises packages/design-tokens/ as one item covering the Problem.type registry, severity.json and this palette — see the finding in the Step 2 report and DIVERGENCES.md.

parity.rule: Every token in `shared` MUST appear in the peer with an identical value. Every token in `portalOnly` MUST NOT appear in the peer. Both directions are asserted, so a value that drifts on either surface fails the build.
parity.hubIsATranscription: pemo_colors.dart is a transcription of design-system section 2, not the normative source. Making a transcription the parity hub means the check catches DRIFT between surfaces but cannot catch all three being wrong together against the design system. That limitation is the finding; the check is the mitigation. Recorded in DIVERGENCES.md.

brand.primary.role: Primary action, active navigation, links, focus accent

brand.deep.role: Sidebar ground, strong headings, pressed state, badge text

brand.tintBorder.role: Border on a brand tint surface

brand.accent.role: Active-navigation indicator and badge ground, ON BRAND GROUND ONLY. 2.21:1 on white — never text on a light surface.

neutral.600.role: Secondary text. USE THIS on the page ground, not neutral.500.

neutral.500.role: Metadata and subdued icon. WHITE GROUNDS ONLY — 4.34:1 on neutral.50 fails AA for normal text.

accent.heading.whyNotInPeer: Design system v2.0 section 2.5 records #E17401 in the management web export and NOT in mobile; the resident-mobile Dart peer does not carry it, and the parity test asserts that absence. The PORTAL export (this surface) also does not use it — its headings are ink. This token is defined and constrained per PID section 3 so the constraint machinery exists and the colour can never leak into a caption; whether the portal applies it to h1 is recorded as an export-vs-PID divergence in DIVERGENCES.md.
accent.heading.constraint: Measures 3.13:1 on white — large-text AA only (WCAG 2.2 1.4.3). Permitted ONLY at h1 size and weight, on white or neutral.25. PROHIBITED in body copy, captions, metadata, labels, chips, links. Expressed as the single `.pemo-page-title` style, never as a raw colour any component can reach.

nonColorSurfaces.$comment: Sidebar states on brand.deep are alpha composites, not palette entries. The export uses rgba white over the deep ground for the active/hover item. Kept here so no component invents them.
